page: Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EBDSv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes a bundled 1843 GB local SSD and is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in memory-intensive and parallelized operations. The server achieves a strong PassMark CPU score of 50758.8 and a PassMark memory score of 2826.39. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is highly efficient at 221.85 GB/sec, and PassMark database operations score at 23567.62, placing these metrics in the top 25%. However, single-core performance remains average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1689.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1900.08.

While the server excels in database operations and memory bandwidth, it exhibits limitations in large-scale machine learning tasks without dedicated GPU hardware. LLM inference text generation for a large 70B model is poor, registering at only 2.33 tokens/sec. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, relational database management systems, caching layers like Redis, and data processing pipelines, rather than heavy deep learning inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure E48bds_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the EBDSv5 family, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz, it includes a 1843 GB local SSD and supports premium block storage. Performance benchmarks show strong results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark database operations, and memory scores, placing these in the top 25%. Conversely, single-core metrics and large-scale LLM inference text generation are average to poor, with 70B model text generation limited to 2.33 tokens/sec. This hardware profile offers high resource density for memory-heavy applications. It is highly recommended for relational databases, enterprise applications, and memory-intensive data processing workloads.
